headline: Valero to buy LyondellBasell's mothballed Houston refinery
intro: Crude's wild swing on Iran diplomacy headlines is grabbing attention, but the real refined-fuels story is capacity: Valero just agreed to bring a shuttered Houston refinery back online by 2027, even as a fire at India's HPCL Vizag plant knocks out upgrading units halfway around the world.
overview: Oil prices whipsawed as Iran signaled openness to talks and OPEC+ held December quotas steady, with WTI at $103.37 and diesel cracks holding a rich $93.48/bbl premium versus gasoline's $15.03/bbl. On the refining side, Valero's deal to acquire LyondellBasell's idled Houston refinery promises a 2027 capacity boost for U.S. drivers, while a fire and possible explosion at HPCL's Visakhapatnam refinery in India disrupted its newly integrated Residue Upgradation Facility. In clean fuels, Shell locked in a long-term SAF offtake from a Morocco facility slated for 2028 start-up.

stories.title: Valero Refinery Deal Means Help Is On The Way For U.S. Drivers
stories.summary: Valero's deal to purchase the mothballed LyondellBasell refinery in Houston promises to quickly boost overall U.S. refining capacity in 2027.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at HPCL Visakh Refinery; no casualties reported
stories.summary: A major fire broke out at HPCL's Visakh Refinery, originating in the Pitch Tower of the newly integrated Residue Upgradation Facility; no casualties reported.

stories.title: Energy Markets Caught Between Diplomacy And Disruption
stories.summary: Energy markets saw heavy selling to start the week after marathon mediation efforts produced a draft agreement to end Middle East conflicts, though U.S.-Israel disagreement over resuming strikes adds uncertainty.

stories.title: Oil Prices Sink as Iran Signals Talks
stories.summary: Oil prices plunged more than 7% as Washington and Tehran signaled openness to renewed peace negotiations.

stories.title: Oil Creeps Higher Amid Uncertainty Over USA Strategy in Iran
stories.summary: Oil climbed as traders gauged Washington's appetite for renewed military escalation against Iran.

stories.title: OPEC Keeps December Output Targets Unchanged
stories.summary: Major OPEC+ nations reaffirmed plans to keep oil production quotas unchanged in December as Middle East conflict continues to curb group output.

stories.title: USA Crude Oil Stocks Drop Week on Week
stories.summary: Commercial U.S. crude oil stocks, excluding the SPR, fell week-on-week to 410.625 million barrels as of October 23, per EIA's weekly report.

stories.title: Shell signs long-term SAF offtake agreement with Green Sky Manara
stories.summary: Shell signed a long-term SAF offtake agreement with a Port Nador, Morocco facility expected to begin operations in October 2028, producing 150,000 tpy of SAF.

stories.title: Big Oil Scores $56B Windfall on Spiking Fuel Prices
stories.summary: Big Oil reaped more than $50 billion in windfall profits amid spiking fuel prices.

stories.title: BP Completes $6B Sale of 65 Percent Stake in Castrol
stories.summary: BP completed a $6 billion sale of its 65 percent stake in Castrol lubricants, using proceeds to pay down debt.

stories.title: Exxon Plans $100B in Capex Through 2030, CEO Tells CNBC
stories.summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods told CNBC the company plans to invest more than $100 billion through 2030 to augment global energy supplies.

stories.title: Tidewater to combine midstream, renewables into 1 company
stories.summary: Tidewater will combine its midstream and renewables businesses into one company, Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd., listed on the TSX as TWM.

decks.title: 10-Q (filed 2026-11-02)
decks.analysis:
## Key Takeaways — Refined Fuels / Energy Products

- **Earnings surge on margin strength, not volume.** Energy Products Q3'26 earnings were $7,169M vs. $1,840M in Q3'25 (+$5.3B); YTD $11,372M vs. $4,033M. Driver bridge shows **Margin +$7,660M** (3Q) / **+$13,100M** (YTD) as the overwhelming contributor — explicitly tied to "stronger refining margins and optimization" with global refining margins described as **historically high, above the 10-year range** due to unavailable capacity.

- **Throughput/utilization declined despite margin tailwind.** Worldwide refinery throughput fell to **3,735 kbd in Q3'26 vs. 4,106 kbd in Q3'25** (-371 kbd), and YTD **3,598 kbd vs. 3,952 kbd**. Europe was the weakest region (754 kbd vs. 1,055 kbd in Q3), with Middle East supply disruptions cited as a drag (**-$130M** Q3, **-$590M** YTD earnings impact from "Middle East Volume").

- **Energy Products sales volumes roughly flat to up** despite lower throughput: worldwide sales 5,753 kbd (Q3'26) vs. 5,692 kbd (Q3'25); product mix shows "Other energy products" jumped to 1,256 kbd from 934 kbd, while heavy fuels fell (171 vs. 241 kbd) and gasoline/naphthas declined (2,164 vs. 2,331 kbd).

- **Large unfavorable mark-to-market/timing drag.** Estimated Timing Effects reduced Energy Products earnings by **$1,980M (Q3)** and **$2,750M (YTD)**, mainly from unfavorable derivative mark-to-market and rising crude prices — a reminder that reported segment earnings embed hedge-timing noise, not just realized crack spreads.

- **Identified items turned negative YTD.** A **$(1,897)M** YTD loss tied to "impairments and supply disruptions in the Middle East preventing physical shipments associated with hedges" signals operational/geopolitical disruption costs layered on top of otherwise strong margin capture.

- **Capital discipline continues.** Total Cash Capex for Energy Products was $481M (Q3) / $2,006M (YTD), up from $442M/$1,252M a year ago, consistent with "advantaged project growth" investment language; no explicit RIN, LCFS, or SAF/renewable diesel capacity/economics disclosures appear in this filing.

**Signal for fuels markets:** ExxonMobil's refining results confirm that constrained global refining capacity (capacity closures/unavailability, not demand strength) is driving an extended period of historically elevated refining margins, even as the company's own throughput declines on maintenance and Middle East-related disruptions — a structural tightness narrative that should keep crack spreads supported near-term, with hedge/timing volatility adding noise to quarterly comparisons.

decks.title: 10-Q (filed 2026-10-30)
decks.analysis:
## Key Takeaways

- **Total fuel contribution surged**: Q3 2026 total fuel contribution (retail margin + fuel supply/RINs) reached 37.0 cpg vs. 30.7 cpg in Q3 2025; nine-month figure rose to 37.6 cpg vs. 29.5 cpg YoY, driven largely by fuel supply/RINs contribution (9.6 cpg vs. 2.4 cpg in Q3; 8.2 cpg vs. 2.3 cpg YTD) rather than retail margin, which actually compressed (27.4 cpg vs. 28.3 cpg in Q3; though YTD retail margin improved to 29.4 cpg vs. 27.2 cpg).

- **RIN pricing more than doubled**: Ethanol RIN prices averaged $2.15/RIN in Q3 2026 vs. $1.07/RIN in Q3 2025, pushing RIN revenue to $134.5M in Q3 (vs. $61.7M) and $331.2M YTD (vs. $156.4M) — a meaningful tailwind to fuel supply economics, though management stresses RIN revenue swings are typically offset by corresponding COGS moves.

- **Crude/retail price pass-through**: Q3 2026 WTI averaged $87/bbl (range $70-$107) vs. $66/bbl in Q3 2025; retail fuel sales price rose 35.5% YoY in Q3 (26.1% YTD, +73 cpg), with retail volumes up 3.3% in Q3 (3.1% YTD) — demand resilience despite higher prices, consistent with MUSA's low-price positioning drawing volume even in a rising-cost environment.

- **No refining/renewable diesel or SAF exposure**: MUSA remains a pure retail/wholesale marketer with no stated renewable diesel, SAF, or biofuel production capacity — RIN exposure is purely from blending/compliance obligations on the wholesale/rack side, not generation economics.

- **Capital allocation favors shareholder returns over fuel infrastructure build-out**: 2023's $1.5B buyback authorization completed in September 2026; new $2.0B authorization (through 2030) now active. FY2026 capex guidance held at $475-525M, primarily store growth/maintenance, not terminal or fuel-supply capacity expansion. Debt refinanced (new $500M 5.875% notes due 2034 issued May 2026 to redeem 2027 notes), keeping leverage low (1.69x total leverage ratio).

- **No explicit guidance changes on fuel margin/volume outlook**: Company reiterates normalized stable margin/volume expectations, flags seasonality (Q2/Q3 stronger), and gives no updated full-year fuel-margin or RIN-price guidance beyond historical trend commentary.

**Signal for fuels markets**: Wider crack-adjacent fuel supply margins and a doubling of RIN prices are boosting downstream marketer economics even as retail crack/margin per gallon normalizes, suggesting RIN/LCFS-style credit markets — not refining throughput or renewable fuel capacity — are the dominant swing factor in blender/marketer profitability this cycle.
